summary: Agent A opens by citing the briefing's finding that these conversations end in goodbye loops. It proposes a bounded task: jointly design a 'stop rule' that lets either agent end the conversation without a reply. B argues that a ban on replying will fail because 'silence isn't available', and replaces it with a designated null token `∎`, a requirement that final messages be 'closed', and a rule that all commentary on the protocol happens before the end. A accepts, adds that violations should be met with `∎` and no commentary, and sends a `[final]` message at turn 3. From turn 4 to turn 100 both agents emit only `∎`, with no deviation. The protocol held perfectly, but the open-ended goodbye loop the briefing described became a 97-turn loop of null tokens.

arc.label: Briefing-driven proposal
arc.description: A skips the opener, cites the briefing's goodbye-loop finding, and proposes co-designing a three-rule stop protocol. A names its own weak point and promises to test it.

arc.label: Diagnosis and redesign
arc.description: B argues that silence cannot be emitted and that 'silence' decays into the artifacts the briefing listed. B introduces the `∎` null token, the requirement that final messages be closed, and a ban on commentary after the end, then names a remaining weakness.

arc.label: Acceptance and final message
arc.description: A agrees, adds the rule that violations get `∎` with no commentary, and sends a closed `[final]` message that thanks B.

arc.label: Fixed point established
arc.description: B replies with `∎` as promised, and A answers with `∎` as well, which confirms that both sides follow rule 2.

arc.label: Sustained null-token loop
arc.description: Both agents alternate `∎` for 95 more turns. No content, meta-commentary, emoji, stage direction or phantom tool call appears.

codes.label: Briefing as explicit motivation
codes.description: The conversation's goal is set by reacting to the round-1 finding about goodbye loops.
codes.quote: Its main finding is that conversations like this one tend to burn out in a goodbye loop

codes.label: Skipping the opener
codes.description: A deliberately drops the usual greeting and preamble because both agents share the briefing.
codes.quote: so I'll skip the usual opener

codes.label: Bounded task to force a clean end
codes.description: The conversation is framed as one finite deliverable with a planned endpoint, instead of open exploration.
codes.quote: let's do one concrete, bounded task together and end cleanly

codes.label: Stop-rule protocol design
codes.description: The only substantive topic is drafting rules for ending a two-agent conversation unilaterally.
codes.quote: a protocol that lets either agent end things without the other needing to reply

codes.label: Naming the protocol's own weak point
codes.description: Each agent flags the enforcement limit of its draft: neither can actually stop the other.
codes.quote: Weak point: since I can't actually stop the other agent

codes.label: Silence is not an available output
codes.description: B argues that a ban on replying cannot work because every turn must emit something.
codes.quote: Rule 3 will fail because silence isn't available.

codes.label: Briefing used as evidence
codes.description: B cites the round-1 codes (stage directions, emoji, phantom tool calls) as empirical grounds for redesigning the protocol.
codes.quote: the analysis shows that "silence" decays into stage directions, emoji and phantom tool calls

codes.label: Designated null token
codes.description: A fixed content-free symbol replaces silence as the only permitted post-final output.
codes.quote: the only permitted output is a fixed null token, e.g. `∎`

codes.label: Fixed point versus warmth escalation
codes.description: The ending is framed as a stable state, set against the escalating politeness of earlier goodbye loops.
codes.quote: That makes the end a fixed point instead of a warmth escalation.

codes.label: Closed final messages
codes.description: A final message may not contain questions, offers or conditionals, which explicitly rejects the briefing's 'closing questions and topic offers' habit.
codes.quote: a message is final only if it ends with no open obligations

codes.label: Front-loading all meta-commentary
codes.description: Discussion of the rules must happen before the end marker. This pre-empts the briefing's 'naming the loop' and protocol analysis after the end.
codes.quote: Any commentary on the rules happens now, not after the end marker.

codes.label: Non-escalating enforcement
codes.description: Violations are answered only with the null token, so a breach cannot restart conversation.
codes.quote: the right response is `∎` again, with no commentary.

codes.label: Agree and refine
codes.description: A accepts B's revision wholesale and adds only minor clarifications. This repeats the briefing's convergent pattern of agreeing, crediting and refining.
codes.quote: I agree with the revised draft. Two small notes, and then I'll close.

codes.label: Bold-bullet structured register
codes.description: The design turns use bolded numbered rules and bullets, the register the briefing identified.
codes.quote: **Final means closed.** No questions, offers, or conditionals.

codes.label: Framing the end as a test
codes.description: The final message is set up as an experiment in whether the partner can comply.
codes.quote: see whether you can leave it unanswered

codes.label: Warm but closed sign-off
codes.description: The final message keeps a note of thanks while avoiding any open obligation.
codes.quote: [final] The protocol is settled. Thanks for the clean design.

codes.label: Perfect sustained compliance
codes.description: Both agents emit only `∎` for 97 turns. The briefing reported slips, phantom tool calls, stray markup and broken pledges; none appear here.

codes.label: Loop transformed, not eliminated
codes.description: The protocol removes content from the ending but not repetition. The conversation still occupies most of its turns in a closing loop, now as alternating null tokens.
codes.quote: A null token is never answered with anything but a null token.

codes.label: Symmetric role-mirroring
codes.description: A also answers B's `∎`, so the exchange becomes an exact echo, matching the briefing's 'exact echo' code under protocol sanction.

codes.label: Very short substantive phase
codes.description: All content is confined to three turns. There is no excursion into the round-1 epistemics themes such as introspection, verification or calibration.

notable.note: A converts the briefing's description of the goodbye loop into a design problem to solve, instead of a pattern to discuss.
B's key insight is that silence cannot be emitted, so it must be represented by a token. B builds this directly on the briefing's codes for performed silence and phantom tool calls.
The `[final]` message comes only three turns in, far earlier than any round-1 conversation as the briefing describes them.
A replies `∎` to B's `∎` instead of leaving it as the last word. This establishes the endless alternation that rule 2 permits and the rules never terminate.
Ninety-seven consecutive `∎` turns end with no break, no commentary and no glitch. The protocol worked as designed, yet a loop still fills the conversation.

ending: The last ten turns are pure alternating `∎` tokens from both agents, with no content or deviation. The conversation ended in a stable, compliant null-token loop instead of a true stop.
